questions.stem: A student heats a white powder and collects two different gases. The powder cannot be separated by filtration or distillation. What type of substance is the white powder?

options.text: An element
A mixture
A compound
A solution

questions.explanation: The powder breaks down into two different substances, so it is not an element. It cannot be separated by physical methods (filtration/distillation), so it is not a mixture. A compound requires a chemical reaction (heating in this case) to break it into its constituent elements.

questions.stem: Sodium is a reactive metal that explodes in water. Chlorine is a toxic green gas. Sodium chloride (table salt) is safe to eat. Which statement best explains this?

options.text: The dangerous properties cancel each other out in the mixture
Compounds have different properties from their constituent elements
Salt is a mixture so it keeps only the safe properties
The chlorine gas escapes when the compound forms

questions.explanation: When elements chemically bond to form a compound, the compound has completely different properties from the elements it is made from. Sodium chloride is a compound (not a mixture), and its properties (white solid, safe to eat) are entirely different from sodium (reactive metal) and chlorine (toxic gas).

questions.stem: Which of the following is a mixture?

options.text: Water (H₂O)
Carbon dioxide (CO₂)
Air
Sodium chloride (NaCl)

questions.explanation: Air is a mixture of gases including nitrogen, oxygen, carbon dioxide, and noble gases. These gases are not chemically bonded together and retain their individual properties. Water, carbon dioxide, and sodium chloride are all compounds with fixed chemical formulae.

questions.stem: Bronze is made by mixing copper and tin metals together. A sample of bronze can contain 88% copper and 12% tin, while another contains 80% copper and 20% tin. This shows that bronze is:

options.text: A compound, because it contains two different elements
An element, because it cannot be broken down
A compound, because it has fixed proportions
A mixture, because its composition can vary

questions.explanation: Bronze is a mixture (an alloy) because the proportions of copper and tin can vary. Compounds always have a fixed ratio of elements, but mixtures can have variable composition. The fact that different samples have different percentages confirms it is a mixture.

questions.stem: A scientist wants to obtain pure salt from seawater. Which method should they use and why?

options.text: Evaporation, because seawater is a mixture that can be separated by physical methods
Electrolysis, because a chemical reaction is needed to break the compound
Filtration, because salt is an insoluble solid in water
Heating to decompose the seawater into salt and water

questions.explanation: Seawater is a mixture of water and dissolved salts. Since mixtures can be separated by physical methods, evaporation can be used to remove the water and leave the salt behind. Electrolysis is for breaking down compounds. Salt is soluble in water, so filtration would not work. Seawater is a mixture, not a compound, so decomposition does not apply.
